title: Measuring correlations using local and nonlocal quenches
authors: Alexey G. Mikhaylenko, Andrew G. Semenov
abstract: We present a theoretical proposal for measuring correlation functions in a quantum field system based on the use of quantum quenches. Using the examples of massive and massless scalar field theories, we show that a short-term perturbation of the system leads to a dependence of the further evolution of the average field on the initial state's correlation functions. Considering two types of perturbations, namely local and nonlocal quenches, we show which correlation functions can be measured in each of these cases. The proposed procedure can be applied to study non-Gaussian correlations.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to measure initial state correlation functions in quantum field theories using controlled quantum quenches. By analyzing the time evolution of the average field after applying local or nonlocal perturbations, the authors show that these measurements can systematically extract information about initial state correlations, including non-Gaussian ones. The method is rigorously derived for free scalar fields, suggesting a powerful diagnostic tool for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper proposes a theoretical method to measure initial state correlation functions in a quantum field system by analyzing the evolution of the average field after applying quantum quenches.
main_result: Local quenches allow measuring initial state averages $\langle \hat{\varphi}_S^n angle$, while nonlocal quenches are necessary to probe higher-order, non-Gaussian correlations of the initial state.
method: The method involves calculating the time evolution of the average field $\langle \hat{\varphi}(t, \vec{x}) angle_Q$ following a quench perturbation $\hat{V}$, which is related to the initial state correlations via the smeared retarded Green's function.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on free real scalar field theories (massive or massless) in $d$-dimensional space, described by a standard Hamiltonian.
key_observables: The average field $\langle \hat{\varphi}(t, \vec{x}) angle_Q$ and the smeared retarded Green's function $G_R^S(t-t_Q, \vec{x}-\vec{x}_Q)$.
important_parameters: The mass $M$ (massive vs. massless), the time difference $t-t_Q$, and the smearing parameter $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The method is strictly applicable only to non-interacting (free) theories; for interacting systems, higher-order non-equilibrium QFT methods are required.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of the retarded Green's function for massive and massless theories in $d=1$, and show the time/space dependence of the average field after both local and nonlocal quenches.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by first analyzing the local quench case to extract initial state averages, then extends the formalism to nonlocal quenches to access non-Gaussian correlations, and finally discusses the asymptotic behavior for massive and massless theories.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable theoretical tool—using quench dynamics—to experimentally probe complex, non-Gaussian initial correlations in quantum many-body systems, bridging theoretical QFT with experimental measurement techniques.
